methods.label: Expand the two compositions
methods.explanation:
Compute both compositions to see whether the equation can depend on \(x\). Substituting \(g(x)\) into \(f\) gives
\[
f(g(x))=m(px+q)+n=mpx+mq+n.
\]
Similarly,
\[
g(f(x))=p(mx+n)+q=pmx+pn+q.
\]
Since \(mp=pm\), the terms involving \(x\) are equal and cancel. The equation is therefore equivalent to
\[
mq+n=pn+q,
\]
or
\[
n(1-p)-q(1-m)=0.
\]
This condition contains no \(x\). If it holds, every real \(x\) satisfies the original equation. If it fails, no real \(x\) does. All steps remain valid when any coefficient is zero, since no division by a coefficient was used. Thus a solution exists if and only if the condition in choice D holds.
